      Korea FA release Paik Seung-ho statement after Birmingham City set-back

      Birmingham City have six players away on international duty but Paik Seung-ho is reported to have left the South Korea camp

      Comments
      Sport
      Brian Dick Reach Football Correspondent
      09:55, 29 Sep 2026Updated 11:35, 29 Sep 2026

      Paik Seung-ho has withdrawn from the South Korea squad after picking up an injury on international duty.

      That’s according to reports in South Korea which claim the Blues midfielder is one of two players who have been forced out.

      Paik, who has played in all ten Blues matches so far this season, had been with Robert Moreno’s squad for the matches with Ecuador, Uruguay, Venezuela and Uzbekistan.

      Having sat on the bench for the 3-0 win over Ecuador the 29-year-old was not in the match-day squad in the 4-1 loss to Uruguay.

      ‌

      FOLLOW ON FACEBOOK! All the latest Blues news on Birmingham Live’s Birmingham City FC Facebook page

      South Korean outlets Star News and Chosun Biz are reporting Paik and Midtjylland’s Cho Gue-sung have left the national set-up.

      Speaking after the Uruguay game Moreno revealed two players had dropped out and today’s articles cite an announcement by the Korea Football Association as saying: "Following a meeting with the coaching staff and medical team, it was determined that Paik Seung-ho needs to recover rather than play in the remaining matches. For the protection of the player, he is scheduled to return to his club team.”

      The nature or extent of the injury is not specified.

      ‌

      One good thing about the extended international break is that Blues do not play again until October 10, when they make the short trip to West Brom.

      Chris Davies would certainly rather have a player he has relied upon for the bulk of his tenure at St Andrew’s although Paik has slipped out of the starting line-up in recent games.

      Jhon Solis and Tomoki Iwata have started the last two games, with Paik playing the full 90 in only two of Blues’ eight Championship games so far this season.

      Davies is also hoping to have his midfield options bolstered by the return of Max Bird, although Solis is also currently away on international duty with Colombia.
